title: Two selected CHIME bursts retain a higher later peak above 20 MHz in both catalog fits
abstract: We compare first-to-last component peak-frequency differences in CHIME/FRB Catalogs 1 and 2. In 29 selected matched events, a 1 MHz sign guard gives 18 lower-later pairs, five higher-later pairs and three sign changes; three events are neutral in at least one release. Two events retain higher later peaks above 20 MHz with all fitted peaks between 410 and 790 MHz: FRB20181222E and FRB20190605B. Both retain component count and pass endpoint-time and S/N controls. No event retains a rise of at least 40 MHz in both releases. The result tests processing stability for the same observations. It does not confirm intrinsic upward drift or a new phenomenon. Peak errors, model covariance, beam calibration and independent telescope observations were not tested. Code, aggregate results, input hashes and external retrieval steps are included. External record tables remain outside the baseline package.

display.caption: Fitted endpoint directions for 29 matched events and counts under minimum-difference cuts. Both releases use the same observations.

citations.reason: Its higher-later candidates motivate a new cross-release stability test. No code or derived rows are reused.
Its same-event DM revision control motivates this peak-direction control.
